Aggregate PRIO-GRID values to supplied country boundaries

Source: R/pg_to_country.R
pg_to_country.Rd

Builds a reproducible cell-to-country crosswalk from user-supplied country polygons and transfers values using explicit extensive or intensive semantics. Supplying boundaries keeps the territorial definition and date under the researcher's control. A single boundary definition is used per call; historical panels with changing borders should be processed by boundary vintage and then combined explicitly.

Usage

pg_to_country(
  data,
  countries,
  country_id,
  values,
  variable_type,
  pgid = "pgid",
  time = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  assignment = c("fractional", "largest", "centroid"),
  na_rm = FALSE,
  return_crosswalk = FALSE,
  config = priogrid::pg_current_config()
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing cell-level values.

countries

An sf object containing country polygons.

country_id

Name of the country identifier column.

values

Names of numeric value columns.

variable_type

"extensive" or "intensive", either once for all variables or as a named vector.

pgid

Name of the cell-ID column in data.

time

Optional temporal key column.

group

Optional additional grouping columns.

assignment

Cell assignment method passed to pg_crosswalk().

na_rm

Should missing source values be ignored?

return_crosswalk

Return only the aggregated data or a list containing both data and the generated crosswalk?

config

A PRIO-GRID configuration object.

Value

A data frame, or a list when return_crosswalk = TRUE.

Examples

config <- priogrid::pg_config(nrow = 18, ncol = 36)
countries <- pg_geometry(342:344, config = config)
countries$country <- c("a", "a", "b")
x <- data.frame(pgid = 342:344, population = c(10, 20, 30))
pg_to_country(
  x, countries, "country", "population", "extensive",
  config = config
)
#>   country population population_coverage
#> 1       a         30                   1
#> 2       b         30                   1
